description: Canonical vendor-neutral onboarding and bootstrap package for Iceberg Playbook.

playbooks.name: Getting Started
playbooks.description: Canonical onboarding procedures and baseline operational workflows for the Iceberg Support Playbook system.

sops.title: How to Use Playbooks
sops.purpose: Explain how to find, open, and navigate Playbooks and their operational content.
sops.whenToUse: For new users learning how knowledge is organized, or when locating operational content by domain.
requirements: Active access to the Iceberg Support Playbook portal
Appropriate permission to view the relevant Playbook
checklist: Locate the correct Playbook
Review Overview
Navigate Issues / Guides / SOPs
Use search/filter where needed
Open the relevant operational content

steps.title: Navigate and Find a Playbook
steps.description: Open the Playbooks directory from the main navigation. Browse the available domain cards or use the search field to filter by name. Each card displays the domain description and live counts for child Issues, Guides, and SOPs.
steps.importantNote: Playbooks group all operational materials—common issues, solution guides, and standard operating procedures—by functional product or platform domain.
steps.successIndicator: The target Playbook card is located with its current content counts visible.

steps.title: Open the Playbook Workspace
steps.description: Click the target Playbook tile to enter its workspace. The Overview tab immediately surfaces recent operational activity: Recently Updated items, Common Issues, and Issues flagged as Needs Guide.
steps.successIndicator: The Playbook workspace loads showing the Overview dashboard and active operational sections.

steps.title: Navigate Operational Content
steps.description: Use the Issues, Guides, and SOPs tabs to inspect specific procedures and troubleshooting workflows. Refine lists using the in-playbook search bar or the Verified and Draft status filter. Use the contextual Create action to start a new Issue, Guide, or SOP linked directly to this Playbook.
steps.successIndicator: Relevant operational content is opened for execution or a linked draft is initiated.

sops.escalationRules: If the required operational domain or critical procedure is missing, contact the Support Operations Lead with the proposed scope and required subject-matter expertise.
sops.completionCriteria: The user can locate a Playbook, understand its structure, navigate Issues, Guides, and SOPs, and use search and status filters to find the required content.
sops.internalNotes: Keep onboarding content aligned with the current Playbooks interface and workflow.

revisionHistory.changes: Aligned onboarding content with the current Playbooks interface and navigation flow.

sops.title: How to Use Issues
sops.purpose: Explain how to find, review, and document Issues and access their related solution Guides within a Playbook.
sops.whenToUse: When investigating a known problem, reviewing symptoms and diagnostic requirements, or documenting a newly identified Issue.
requirements: Active access to the Iceberg Support Playbook portal
Appropriate Support or Admin permission for create or edit actions
checklist: Locate the relevant Issue
Use search or status filters when needed
Review symptoms and diagnostic information
Open the related Solution Guide if available
Create or update the Issue when appropriate

steps.title: Locate and Filter Issues
steps.description: Open the relevant Playbook and select the Issues tab, or use Quick Access or Global Search to locate an Issue across Playbooks. Use the in-playbook search field and the All, Verified, or Draft status filters to narrow the results. Issue rows show key information such as the Issue code, title, status, difficulty, and Jira Code when available.
steps.successIndicator: The relevant Issue is identified with its current status and key metadata visible.

steps.title: Review Issue Details and Diagnostics
steps.description: Open the Issue to review its Problem Summary, Symptoms, Error Message or Code, context, affected area, and Information to Collect. Use these details to understand the problem and the diagnostic information required.
steps.successIndicator: The Issue symptoms, context, and required diagnostic information have been reviewed.

steps.title: Use the Solution Guide or Document New Knowledge
steps.description: Review the Solution Guide section on the Issue page. If a Guide is available, use Open Guide to access the resolution steps. If the Issue needs a Guide, use Create Guide to begin documenting the solution. If the problem does not yet exist as an Issue, use Create Issue from the Playbook workspace or Create hub.
steps.successIndicator: The related Guide is opened for execution, or a new Issue or Guide draft is started when needed.

sops.escalationRules: If an operational problem has no matching Issue, lacks required diagnostic information, or requires urgent escalation, contact the Support Operations Lead with the known symptoms and affected area.
sops.completionCriteria: The user can locate an Issue, understand its symptoms and diagnostic requirements, access its related Guide, and create or update Issue records when permitted.
sops.internalNotes: Issues describe diagnosed problems and symptoms. Step-by-step resolutions should be maintained in linked Guides.

revisionHistory.changes: Aligned onboarding content with the current Issues interface and Guide workflow.

sops.title: How to Use Guides
sops.purpose: Explain how to locate, follow, verify, and maintain solution Guides linked to diagnosed Issues.
sops.whenToUse: When following a documented solution, reviewing prerequisites or troubleshooting notes, or creating and updating solution documentation.
requirements: Active access to the Iceberg Support Playbook portal
Access to the relevant Playbook and Guide
Appropriate Support or Admin permission for create, edit, restore, or delete actions
checklist: Locate the relevant Guide
Confirm the linked Issue and prerequisites
Follow the numbered solution steps
Review Common Problems and supporting media when needed
Check Version History or update the Guide when appropriate

steps.title: Locate the Guide and Linked Issue
steps.description: Open the relevant Playbook and select the Guides tab, use Global Search, or open the Guide directly from an Issue's Solution Guide section. Use search and the All, Verified, or Draft status filters to narrow the results. When the Guide opens, confirm its parent Playbook and linked Issue.
steps.successIndicator: The correct Guide is open and its linked Issue and current status are confirmed.

steps.title: Review Prerequisites and Follow the Solution
steps.description: Review Before You Start and Important Information before beginning. Follow the numbered steps in order, using screenshots, videos, PDF references, Important Notes, and Success Indicators where provided. Confirm the expected result before moving to the next step.
steps.successIndicator: The Guide steps are completed in sequence and the documented expected results are verified.

steps.title: Resolve Blockers and Review Guide History
steps.description: If a step does not work as expected, review the Common Problems section for documented causes and solutions. Use Version History to inspect previous Guide versions and change summaries. When permitted, use Edit Guide, document what changed, preview the update, and publish a new version. Older versions can be restored non-destructively as a new current version.
steps.successIndicator: The blocker is resolved, or the Guide history is reviewed and an appropriate update or version restore is completed.

sops.escalationRules: If a verified Guide produces reproducible errors, requires an urgent update after an upstream platform change, or the linked Issue has no usable solution, contact the Guide Author or Support Operations Lead.
sops.completionCriteria: The user can locate a Guide, confirm its linked Issue, follow and verify its solution steps, use troubleshooting resources, inspect Version History, and update or restore Guides when permitted.
sops.internalNotes: Guides contain canonical step-by-step solutions for diagnosed Issues. Publishing an update creates a non-destructive version snapshot and preserves the Guide history.

revisionHistory.changes: Aligned onboarding content with the current Guides workflow, Issue relationship, and version history.

sops.title: How to Use SOPs
sops.purpose: Explain how to locate, follow, verify, and maintain Standard Operating Procedures using checklists, process steps, supporting media, and escalation guidance.
sops.whenToUse: When executing a repeatable operational workflow, checking prerequisites, tracking a multi-stage process, or creating and updating standard operating procedures.
requirements: Active access to the Iceberg Support Playbook portal
Access to the relevant Playbook and SOP
Appropriate Support or Admin permission for create or edit actions
checklist: Locate the relevant SOP
Confirm its Purpose, When to Use, and Responsible Team
Complete Before You Start prerequisites
Track progress using the Process Checklist
Follow process steps and verify Expected Results
Review Escalation Rules or update the SOP when appropriate

steps.title: Locate and Review the SOP
steps.description: Open the relevant Playbook and select the SOPs tab, use Global Search, or use the SOPs Quick Access entry on Home. Use search and the All, Verified, or Draft status filters to locate the procedure. Open the SOP and review its Purpose, When to Use, Responsible Team, and estimated duration to confirm it applies to the task.
steps.successIndicator: The correct SOP is open and its operational scope and ownership are confirmed.

steps.title: Check Prerequisites and Follow the Procedure
steps.description: Review and complete the Before You Start requirements, then use the interactive Process Checklist to track workflow progress. Follow each numbered Process Step in order, reviewing Important Notes, screenshots, inline videos, PDF references, and Expected Results where provided.
steps.successIndicator: The required checklist items and process steps are completed with expected results verified.

steps.title: Verify Completion and Maintain the SOP
steps.description: Review the Completion Criteria before finishing the procedure. If a blocker occurs, consult the Escalation Rules and Related Resources. Authorized users can use Edit to update requirements, checklist items, process steps, or media. Review Version History to understand previously documented changes.
steps.successIndicator: The completion criteria are verified, or an appropriate escalation or SOP update is started.

sops.escalationRules: If an operational procedure produces recurring failures, has outdated prerequisites, or a critical workflow lacks an appropriate SOP, contact the Support Operations Lead or responsible SOP team.
sops.completionCriteria: The user can locate an SOP, review its scope and prerequisites, track progress with interactive checklists, follow and verify process steps with supporting media, and update the SOP when permitted.
sops.internalNotes: SOPs document repeatable operational procedures and workflows. Use Guides for step-by-step technical troubleshooting solutions to diagnosed Issues.

revisionHistory.changes: Aligned onboarding content with the current SOP workflow, interactive checklists, media support, and editing experience.

sops.title: How to Manage Users
sops.purpose: Explain how Admins can invite team members, assign appropriate roles, manage account access, create password reset links, and use built-in administrative safeguards.
sops.whenToUse: When onboarding a new team member, changing a user's role, disabling or re-enabling access, creating a password reset link, or reviewing user and invitation status.
requirements: Active access to the Iceberg Support Playbook portal
Admin role assigned to your account
checklist: Open the Users console
Review user roles and account statuses
Invite new users with the appropriate role and link expiry
Copy and securely share generated activation links
Manage roles, account access, or password reset links when needed
Observe self-protection and last-admin safeguards

steps.title: Open User Management and Review Access
steps.description: Open Users from the Admin-only sidebar navigation. Review the unified user table showing names, email addresses, roles, statuses, invitation expiry details, and available actions. The available roles are Viewer, Support, and Admin, while account states include Active, Disabled, Pending Invite, and Invite Expired.
steps.importantNote: Admin-only procedure: Only users with the Admin role can access User Management.
steps.successIndicator: The Users console is open and current account roles and statuses are understood.

steps.title: Invite a User and Share the Activation Link
steps.description: Select Invite user and enter the user's email address, full name, role, and link expiry. Assign the least-privilege role appropriate for the user's responsibilities. After the invitation is created, copy the activation link from the result dialog and share it securely with the user. The generated link is shown only once in the interface.
steps.successIndicator: The invitation is created with the correct role and expiry, and the activation link is ready to be shared securely.

steps.title: Manage Roles, Access, and Password Links
steps.description: Use the contextual actions on a user row to change roles, disable or enable account access, or create a password reset link. Pending invitations can be resent or revoked. The system prevents an Admin from disabling or demoting their own account and also protects the last active Admin from being disabled or demoted.
steps.successIndicator: The required user access action is completed while administrative safeguards remain intact.

sops.escalationRules: If an invitation cannot be redeemed, account access cannot be restored through the available console actions, or an urgent administrative access issue cannot be resolved safely, contact the Lead Administrator or Support Operations Lead.
sops.completionCriteria: The Admin can review the user roster, invite new users with the appropriate role and expiry, securely share activation links, manage account roles and access, create password reset links, and understand the built-in administrative safeguards.
sops.internalNotes: User accounts are not deleted from User Management. Use Disable to revoke access while preserving authorship, history, and audit records. The system protects both the current Admin account and the last active Admin from accidental lockout.

revisionHistory.changes: Initial canonical onboarding release with Admin-only safeguards.
Aligned onboarding content with the current Users console, invitation workflow, role management, password links, and administrative safeguards.
